# Parvaz

> A Farsi-first Android **browser tunnel** that routes Chrome (and other
> Chromium browsers) traffic through a user-deployed Google Apps Script
> relay, using TLS SNI concealment and a local on-device MITM to terminate
> TLS for re-encapsulation. Needs Android 11 or later and a 64-bit ARM
> phone. Monorepo: Kotlin front end + Go sidecar. Follows the architecture
> of MasterHttpRelayVPN-RUST with different UX.

## Overview

Parvaz ships as one APK. Inside: a Kotlin/Compose UI (Farsi default),
Android `VpnService` subclass, `tun2socks`, and a Go sidecar
(`libparvaz.so`) that runs a local SOCKS5 on `127.0.0.1:1080`. The
sidecar routes each connection one of three ways: direct, SNI rewrite
(for some Google-owned hosts, which still needs the browser to trust the
Parvaz certificate), or **MITM-interception**, which reconstructs the HTTP
request and sends it through the Apps Script relay wrapped in a JSON
envelope (`{k, m, u, h, b?, ct?, r}`). The routing rules match host names,
but the Android tunnel hands the sidecar IP addresses, so today HTTPS
connections, Google sites included, take the MITM relay path.

Scope is deliberately browser-only — non-browser Android apps
(Instagram, WhatsApp, banking, streaming) reject user-installed CAs and
will not tunnel through MITM. Documented honestly in README.md and
ARCHITECTURE.md.

## Technology Stack

- Kotlin 2.3.21 + Jetpack Compose (Material3), min SDK 24 (the tunnel only starts on Android 11 / API 30 or later), target SDK 36
- Go 1.24+ (stdlib-first; deps: `github.com/andybalholm/brotli`, `github.com/klauspost/compress/zstd`)
- Android VpnService API + tun2socks
- Gradle 9.5.1 (Kotlin DSL) + AGP 9.2.1
- Google Apps Script runtime (user-deployed, free tier, 20,000 URL fetches/day per account)
- Light-theme NOTAM / declassified-briefing aesthetic
- Fonts: Vazirmatn (Persian default), Redaction (Latin display), JetBrains Mono

## Architecture

- `app/` — Kotlin + Compose UI (Farsi-first), VpnService, tun2socks, sidecar launcher, MITM CA install flow, NOTAM theme, settings
- `core/fronter/` — TLS-with-custom-SNI dialer + HTTP/1.1 client
- `core/protocol/` — Apps Script JSON envelope encode/decode
- `core/codec/` — gzip / br / zstd / identity decoders
- `core/relay/` — envelope + fronted client + codec glue
- `core/socks5/` — local SOCKS5 listener
- `core/mitm/` — on-device CA, dynamic leaf certs, TLS interception
- `core/dispatcher/` — routing decision: direct, SNI rewrite or MITM + relay
- `core/cmd/parvazd/` — sidecar main, packaged per-ABI as `libparvaz.so`
- `reference/` — MasterHttpRelayVPN upstream Python, read-only
- `website/` — GitHub Pages (English, Persian, Danish)

## Key Files

- `CLAUDE.md` — architecture, layer rules, required skills, engineering principles
- `PLAN.md` — TDD milestone list
- `ARCHITECTURE.md` — full data path diagram and core/app boundary
- `core/go.mod` — Go module `github.com/cocodedk/parvaz/core`
- `apps_script/Code.gs` — the server Parvaz talks to (deploy to your own Google account)
- `gradle.properties` — also holds VERSION_NAME/VERSION_CODE, the app's version

## Wire Protocol

```
Per tunneled HTTP request:
    TCP connect <google_ip>:443  (default 216.239.38.120)
    TLS handshake  SNI = www.google.com  (DPI-visible)
    POST /macros/s/<DEPLOYMENT_ID>/exec HTTP/1.1
    Host: script.google.com
    Content-Type: application/json
    body = { k, m, u, h, b?, ct?, r }

Response = { s, h, b } or { e: "..." }.

The dispatcher has hostname lists for *.google.com / *.youtube.com / etc.
that skip the envelope (direct TCP, or an SNI rewrite that still
terminates TLS locally). They apply only when the dispatcher receives a
host name. The Android tunnel gives it IP addresses, so assume Google
sites use the relay and its quota too.
```

## Access URL format

`parvaz://<deployment-id>/<access-key>#<optional-display-name>`

Registered URI scheme: tapping a parvaz:// link in a messenger opens Parvaz
directly. The app cannot scan QR codes yet.
